messages:
Anna L: Hey team — urgent last-minute gap for EU night coverage this weekend. I'm out sick and Jorge can't cover 00:00-06:00 UTC on Sunday (the holiday swap fell through). Primary was Jorge, secondary Mike. Can someone take primary for that window? High-priority customer regression test is scheduled 01:00-03:00 UTC so we'd prefer a single primary to avoid split paging.

Mike R: I can help but only from 01:30-05:30 UTC. I have a family thing earlier. If that helps as primary for the customer window at 01:30-03:00?

Sara V: I can do 23:30-02:00 UTC if that covers the start. Not ideal for the full window but can bridge to Mike.

Jorge: Really sorry everyone — my travel plans got canceled but can't move the coverage. Won't be available to take any hours. My bad.

Anna L: No worries Jorge, thanks for confirming. If Mike + Sara can stitch it we should be ok, but who will be the official primary for pager duty (so alerts route correctly)? We need the primary set to avoid double notifications.

pagerduty-bot: Incident routing update: current primary = none, secondary = none. Please set primary before 23:45 UTC to avoid auto-escalation to oncall rotation.

Mike R: Ok I can set myself as primary in PD for 01:30-05:30. Sara can be primary until 02:00 and then hand off to me at 02:00? Does PD support that handoff window? If not we should set Mike as primary for full window and Sara as secondary.

Sara V: PD doesn't allow timed partial primary assignments without manual handoff. I'm happy to act as secondary and do a manual handoff message at 02:00 to @Mike R.

Anna L: Cool. Plan: Mike primary 01:30-05:30, Sara secondary 23:30-02:00 and hand off verbally in this thread at 02:00. If anyone else can cover earlier primary 00:00-01:30 pls shout. If not, notify customers we'll have reduced coverage 00:00-01:30 (no dedicated primary).

Mike R: I'll take it. Setting PD now.

oncall-bot: oncall-bot: Mike R is now primary for eng-oncall from 1980-01-01T01:30:00Z to 1980-01-01T05:30:00Z (scheduled by Mike R). Sara V set as secondary until 02:00 UTC.

Anna L: Thanks Mike & Sara. Quick runbook highlights for whoever is primary — copy of the minimal triage steps for the regression test: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eu-night-oncall

Anna L: ```
TL;DR runbook steps
1) Check customer job status: kubectl -n jobs get pods -l job=customer-regression
2) If failing, collect logs: kubectl logs -n jobs <pod> -c runner > /tmp/regression.log
3) If model backend OOM, go to runtime dashboard -> ModelInstance -> restart instance and watch logs for 2m
4) If paging spikes, disable noncritical batching: config set batching.enabled false --service inference
5) Escalate to infra-sre if node becomes unresponsive: @eng-sre oncall
```

Mike R: Noted. I'll paste the credential snippet and restart commands into the secure runbook note before the window. Also will monitor the customer job every 5m during 01:00-03:00.

Sara V: I'll keep an eye on the early window and post a handoff note at 02:00. Ping me in this thread if anything happens and I'll jump in. :thumbsup:

Anna L: Appreciate it. If anyone else wants to pick up 00:00-01:30 and be primary let us know — otherwise I'll send a short customer update about reduced coverage there.

Mike R: I'll also add a quick checklist to the PD incident so whoever gets alerts knows the priority: 1) check job status 2) capture logs 3) restart model instance if OOM.

Anna L: OK closing the coordination loop — assigning Mike primary, Sara secondary, Jorge not available. I'll update the holiday rota doc. Thanks everyone and sorry for the scramble.

oncall-bot: oncall-bot: Thread annotated: holiday-coverage-swap. Reminder set for Sara V at 02:00 to post handoff.
